Collaboration computing output

Papers by the experiment collaborations ULAKBİM serves, with at least one Turkish author. 2,968 papers, 192,932 citations. Sources: Scopus 31 Jul 2026 · Web of Science 28 Jul 2026.
Counted separately from the TRUBA dashboard — these papers credit the WLCG grid collectively rather than naming ULAKBİM.
why, and what that means for the numbers

They do acknowledge the computing infrastructure ULAKBİM provides. ATLAS thanks "all WLCG partners … the Tier-2 facilities worldwide", with individual contributors listed in a cited document, and CMS thanks "the computing centers and personnel of the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid". ULAKBİM is a WLCG Tier-2 site, so it sits inside that credit — which is also why no acknowledgement-text search can find these papers by name.

They are kept out of the TRUBA total for a different reason: a TRUBA paper names the centre, while a paper here credits the grid as a whole and is equally claimable by every one of the ~170 Tier-2 sites. Both figures are real; adding them would read as a single "papers ULAKBİM enabled" number that the second half cannot support.

One further limit: ULAKBİM's Tier-2 serves all ATLAS and CMS output, not only the Turkish-authored subset counted here. The Turkish-author filter is a proxy for "papers with a Turkish stake", not a measure of which papers the site's cycles touched.

how the credit is worded, and why Belle II is sourced differently

Of the ATLAS articles here, 768 (54%) carry the WLCG/Tier-2 acknowledgement in their own funding text, and 1,133 (77%) of the CMS ones. None names ULAKBİM — the named list lives in the document ATLAS cites. Belle II is the exception and credits "TÜBİTAK ULAKBİM" directly.

Belle II is Scopus-only — a metadata gap, not an absence of Turkish participation. Turkey does take part: Mehmet Zeyrek (ORCID 0000-0002-9270-7403, Professor of Physics at Middle East Technical University) is listed on the 2025 and 2026 papers.

He is invisible to every affiliation-based method because the papers print no affiliations at all: the published PDFs carry a flat author list with no institution block, so 76 of these 88 papers record zero affiliations in Scopus — none for any country — and Crossref has none either. The Web of Science corpus available here is selected by Turkish address, so a paper with no address cannot enter it whoever wrote it; a scan of all 10,237 corporate-author records there found no Belle II papers at all. What the papers do carry is ORCIDs, on 422 of 423 authors — which is how the affiliation above was recovered, and the only route by which this segment can be attributed.

The 88 were each checked against Crossref: 84 carry a Belle II collaboration author and the other 4 are Belle II on inspection. ATLAS and CMS use both databases.

The Web of Science corpus has no API available to this project and refreshes only when a new database dump is supplied, so its date will often lag the Scopus one.
